connect.description: Grants the shell's own first-run screen exactly one thing: the connection decision. The screen is served from the bundle (the local asset origin), so it needs no remote grant; the product's front end runs in a different window and never sees this capability. No plugin permission is granted here — the connect window cannot read files, open windows, print, or update anything.

desktop-web.description: Grants the web app (served by the bundled Next server on a loopback port, i.e. a REMOTE origin for Tauri) exactly the app commands it drives: raw-ZPL label transport, the update check/apply pair, and the Wave 38 lane 2 native window commands (open/focus role windows, route marula:// links — geometry persistence is Rust-side window events, not renderer-driven). No plugin permissions are granted to this origin and no core permission is needed to invoke app commands. Since tauri 2.11.1 remote origins are ACL-gated for custom commands too, so without this capability all commands are denied in the real shell. 'main' plus 'subwindow::*' labels: every native role window carries the same remote origin and drives the same command surface (ZPL printing works from ANY window). The remote URLs are EXACT origins, not a 127.0.0.1 wildcard: they are the port candidates the shell binds the Next server to (WEB_PORT_CANDIDATES in src/main.rs, 15435-15439), and the capability test there fails if the two lists drift. A wider grant would hand these commands to any local HTTP server; a ZPL destination is separately restricted to printers the user configured in printers.json, so this grant cannot be turned into a TCP write primitive.
